rationale: The exact entry identifies 'the truth' as God's law functioning as the standard. Ps 119:142 supplies a direct, non-metaphorical equation ('thy law is the truth') that the chapter simply reads at face value and pairs with the parallel 'thy word is truth' (John 17:17). This accounts for the supplied texts with fewer steps than any Christological or propositional alternative: the law/word is first established as the measure, after which Jesus can be called 'the truth' only as its living embodiment. No material claim printed in the entry itself is left unsupported; broader chapter applications (Jesus as Torah-in-flesh, the three titles as one reality, etc.) lie outside glossary scope.
book_core_identification: The truth is God's law (the covenant standard/measure by which all else is weighed).
chapter_only_objections: Jesus is the Torah embodied / law in the flesh (application of the three titles in John 14:6)
the way, the truth and the life are three aspects of one Torah reality
the flaming sword of Genesis 3:24 already binds the three symbols together
prosphatos reading of Hebrews 10:20 as 'freshly-slain way'
strongest_counter_interpretation: In mainstream Christian reading, 'the truth' is first and foremost the self-revelation of God in the person of Jesus Christ (John 14:6), with God's word/gospel/Spirit as secondary extensions; law language is true but not the primary referent.
counter_core_identification: The truth is Jesus Christ himself (personal, incarnate revelation of God).
material_core_denial: The counter denies that the primary/basic referent of 'the truth' is God's law as the standard, relocating the core identification to the person of Christ.
counter_case: John 14:6 places the definite article on Christ personally: 'I am … the truth'
Johannine cluster (1:14, 17; 8:31-32; 18:37) treats truth as embodied in and testified by Jesus
Traditional exegesis therefore ranks Christological identification above the OT law-equation
book_explanatory_advantages: Ps 119:142 is an explicit definitional equation ('thy law is the truth'), not a simile
John 17:17 supplies the parallel equation 'thy word is truth,' allowing law and word to be treated as the same covenant standard
2 John 4 links 'walking in truth' to 'a commandment from the Father,' reinforcing the law/standard reading
The entry requires no extra-textual philosophical move from 'true' to 'Truth' as person; the person is explained later as the standard made flesh
counter_explanatory_advantages: Fits the broader Johannine emphasis on personal revelation and the Spirit of truth
